html:
SMTO-CTX-0006 — Your request is too large for SMTO to plan the task

GUID: 7dc00038-1d57-4e30-8317-e0266b9ddbcb
Slug: task-contract-context-capacity
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: context

What happened

  • Before starting work, SMTO turns your request into a short plan called a Task Contract. Your request and its attachments, plus room for that plan, didn't fit in the model, so no work on the task has started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Send a shorter request, or split it into smaller ones, and attach only the files each one needs. The planning step has to read your whole request and its attachments at once.
  2. Open Settings › Agent behavior › Task Contracts and look at Task Contract maximum output tokens. If it was raised far above its default, lower it. This sets the room kept for the plan, and that room comes out of the same total as your request.
  3. To skip planning, open Options in the message box, turn off Task Contract Compilation, and send your request again. With it off, your request goes straight to the agent, and nothing was done yet, so sending again is safe.

What success looks like

  • The task starts and moves past the planning step.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and ask them to check which model handles Task Contract planning and how much text it can hold. Don't raise output limits to fix this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Task Contract compiler preflight failed: the compiler input plus its reserved output (initial or recovery allowance) exceeds the model context window, so the compiler model call was not sent.

What this means

  • Compiler preflight needs room for the complete Task Contract input plus the compiler output reservation; initial or recovery allowance exceeds the model window. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • Compiler preflight needs room for the complete Task Contract input plus the compiler output reservation; initial or recovery allowance exceeds the model window.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare compiler input, attempted compiler output allowance and effective model window; normal execution output settings govern a different phase.

How to fix it

  • Check the failure facts (context_window_tokens, input_tokens_before_compaction, reserved_output_tokens) against the served capacity of the model routed for Task Contract compilation, and the Task Contract output and auto-recovery settings in Settings › Agent behavior › Task Contracts (native/task_contract.py). Reduce the compiler input (current request and attachments), lower an inflated Task Contract maximum output tokens, or turn off Task Contract Compilation for the conversation; raising output limits only reduces input room.
  • Reduce or split compiler input and attachments. Check the Task Contract output allowance and actual model capacity; normal execution output settings do not own this compiler budget.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Task Contract Output Allowance: task-contracts / task_contract_max_tokens. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The complete compiler request fits before its inference is sent.

What not to do

  • Do not increase max completion tokens as the primary fix; reserving more output reduces input headroom.
  • Do not claim an inference response occurred when the model request did not start.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
